summary: Nike's FY2025 revenue fell to $46.3B from $51.4B the year before, and the stock has dropped from the $60-80 range into the high-$30s over the past year as the market re-rates the turnaround story. This model deliberately does not assume a margin recovery: revenue growth is held to a modest 3%/year and EBITDA margin flat at FY2025's depressed ~9.7% (operating income of $3.7B plus $775M of D&A, both from the 10-K). Even on that conservative, no-turnaround base case, the DCF implies about $43/share against an actual price near $37, suggesting the sell-off has priced in more pessimism than a flat-margin scenario justifies. The sensitivity table shows how much of that gap closes if WACC comes down a point or margins recover even partway toward Nike's historical ~12-13% range.

versions.changelog: Initial publish. Revenue, margin, D&A, capex, and tax rate sourced from Nike's FY2025 10-K (fiscal year ended May 31, 2025); share price and market cap from stockanalysis.com, close of Oct 19, 2026. WACC and all forward growth/terminal assumptions are this model's own estimates, not sourced facts.

summary: Zomato (renamed Eternal Limited in 2024) grew revenue from ₹1,994 cr to ₹20,243 cr over the last five fiscal years, about a 59% CAGR, and only turned durably profitable recently (FY25 EBITDA margin of roughly 3-5%). This model forecasts ten years instead of five, because a company still growing this fast is nowhere near its steady state after five. Growth slows in a straight line from 30% to 8%, and EBITDA margin widens from 6% to 20%. The company holds about ₹16,779 cr more cash than debt, and that cash is added to the equity value. The result is about ₹105 a share against a market price near ₹322. To justify ₹322 you would need growth to stay high for longer, mostly from Blinkit's quick commerce business, and margins to end well above 20%.

versions.changelog: Replaces the first draft, which implied ₹30.14. Two fixes. First, the draft counted ₹2,045 cr of borrowings as net debt and left out the company's cash. Eternal reported a cash balance of ₹18,824 cr at March 31, 2025 (Q4 FY25 shareholder letter), so net cash is ₹18,824 cr minus ₹2,045 cr of debt, or ₹16,779 cr. Second, the forecast now runs ten years instead of five, so growth slows gradually instead of dropping from 15% to the 5% terminal rate in one step. WACC moves from 13% to 12% (risk-free rate near 6.5%, beta about 1.1, equity risk premium about 5%, almost no debt). Revenue and D&A are from the FY25 annual report via screener.in, and the price is the close of Oct 19, 2026. Diluted shares (958 cr) come from FY25 net profit divided by diluted EPS. Capex %, the growth and margin path, and WACC are this model's own estimates.
